title: 2 Kings 15
paragraphs: ¹ In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah became king of Judah. ² He was sixteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jecoliah of Jerusalem. ³ He did what was right in the LORD's eyes, just as his father Amaziah had done. ⁴ Yet the high places were not removed; the people still sacrificed and burned incense there. ⁵ The LORD struck the king with a skin disease, and he remained afflicted until the day he died, living in a separate house. Jotham the king's son was put in charge of the palace and governed the people of the land.

⁶ The rest of the acts of Azariah, and everything he did — are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? ⁷ Azariah rested with his fathers and was buried with them in the City of David, and his son Jotham succeeded him. ⁸ In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah king of Judah, Zachariah son of Jeroboam reigned over Israel in Samaria for six months. ⁹ He did what was evil in the LORD's eyes, just as his fathers had done — he did not turn from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had led Israel into sin. ¹⁰ Shallum son of Jabesh conspired against him, struck him down in public, killed him, and reigned in his place.

¹¹ The rest of the acts of Zachariah are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel. ¹² This fulfilled the word the LORD had spoken to Jehu: "Your descendants will sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation." And so it was. ¹³ Shallum son of Jabesh became king in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah king of Judah, and he reigned in Samaria for one month. ¹⁴ Then Menahem son of Gadi came up from Tirzah to Samaria, struck down Shallum son of Jabesh, killed him, and reigned in his place. ¹⁵ The rest of the acts of Shallum, and the conspiracy he carried out, are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

¹⁶ At that time Menahem attacked Tiphsah and all who were in it and its surrounding region from Tirzah, because they had refused to open their gates to him. He sacked it and ripped open all the pregnant women. ¹⁷ In the thirty-ninth year of Azariah king of Judah, Menahem son of Gadi became king over Israel and reigned for ten years in Samaria. ¹⁸ He did what was evil in the LORD's eyes — throughout his entire reign he did not turn from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had led Israel into sin. ¹⁹ Pul king of Assyria invaded the land, and Menahem gave him a thousand talents of silver to secure his support and strengthen his own grip on the kingdom. ²⁰ Menahem raised this money by taxing all the wealthy men of Israel, fifty shekels of silver from each, to give to the king of Assyria. So the king of Assyria withdrew and did not stay in the land.

²¹ The rest of the acts of Menahem, and everything he did — are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel? ²² Menahem rested with his fathers, and his son Pekahiah succeeded him. ²³ In the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekahiah son of Menahem began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned for two years. ²⁴ He did what was evil in the LORD's eyes — he did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had led Israel into sin. ²⁵ Pekah son of Remaliah, one of his officers, conspired against him and struck him down in the citadel of the royal palace at Samaria, along with Argob and Arieh, aided by fifty men from Gilead. Pekah killed him and reigned in his place.

²⁶ The rest of the acts of Pekahiah, and everything he did, are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel. ²⁷ In the fifty-second year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekah son of Remaliah became king over Israel in Samaria and reigned for twenty years. ²⁸ He did what was evil in the LORD's eyes — he did not turn from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had led Israel into sin. ²⁹ In the days of Pekah king of Israel, Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria came and captured Ijon, Abel-beth-maacah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, and Galilee — all the land of Naphtali — and deported the people to Assyria. ³⁰ Then Hoshea son of Elah conspired against Pekah son of Remaliah, struck him down, killed him, and became king in his place, in the twentieth year of Jotham son of Uzziah.

³¹ The rest of the acts of Pekah, and everything he did, are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel. ³² In the second year of Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel, Jotham son of Uzziah became king of Judah. ³³ He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned for sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jerusha daughter of Zadok. ³⁴ He did what was right in the LORD's eyes, just as his father Uzziah had done. ³⁵ Yet the high places were not removed; the people still sacrificed and burned incense there. He built the Upper Gate of the LORD's temple.

³⁶ The rest of the acts of Jotham, and everything he did — are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? ³⁷ In those days the LORD began sending Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah against Judah. ³⁸ Jotham rested with his fathers and was buried with them in the City of David his father, and his son Ahaz succeeded him.
